instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Yes, Under My Physics
cards.instruction: Agree completely, then redefine each term using rules that make your preferred outcome inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, you may move me forward for the photo. Forward means facing your camera; I'll stay in this shade.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you come two feet closer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Feet are units of zoom. Add two, and I'll tell you when the picture is ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now only your face fits. Is that a full portrait?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. Full means all the important parts, and I decide which those are. You may take it now; you've fitted me in completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll help move your boxes downstairs. Help means saving effort; I'll call the lift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's broken. Will you carry that box yourself?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Yourself means without involving you. You may leave the hiring to me; I'll get a mover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He says he can carry everything if you hold the door. Is that all right?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. Holding means preventing movement. I'll wedge it open. Tell him he may start; I'll supervise from this chair.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: The Logic Gets Bigger
cards.instruction: Use every new detail to expand the impossible system, its history, and the consequences of breaking it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our meeting chairs float at noon. Book the ceiling under my name; they've had landing rights since the first furniture strike.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we stand and tie them down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not on my watch. Restraint broke the last treaty and brought the desks out in sympathy. Get the caretaker to issue an airspace permit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She only issues floor permits. Can we call the ceiling a floor?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only after I recognize it. Turn her plan upside down and bring it here. The last unrecognized floor became cabinet territory; I won't hold this meeting in a filing empire.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Our soup bowl said hello. Use the formal greeting; crockery stopped speaking after the Great Washing-Up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says it wants bread.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Trade has reopened. Offer a roll, but keep the butter separate; mixed gifts caused the gravy embargo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's asking for a seat at dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's recognition as a nation. Move the plates apart before we accidentally concede its borders.

cards.title: Co-Sign This
cards.instruction: Get someone to help by making them an official participant who shares responsibility for the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign beside me before we borrow this barbecue. I'm putting you down as joint custodian.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only offered to carry it. The handle looks cracked. Can we inspect it first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can. As joint custodians. You check the handle; I'll check the legs, and we both sign what we find.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner says we owe her a replacement by Sunday if it breaks. Can I just inspect without borrowing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can lead the inspection. We still return it together. I'll call her about the crack; you stay beside me and confirm what we found before either of us agrees to Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I've made you co-organizer of Saturday's school trip. Can you approve the bus route?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only volunteered to drive. Your route misses the museum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Good catch. Correct it and initial it; then we both own the plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll fix it, but you explain any delays to the parents.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together. I'll introduce you as our transport lead and take the questions beside you.

cards.title: Close It Properly
cards.instruction: Keep them present until both of you complete the ritual that formally ends this role, meeting, or relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you leave book club, we close the discussion together. I'll give the closing line; you answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said goodnight. My taxi's coming. Can we count that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not as the close. I'll say 'chapter closed'; you say 'until next time.' Then you're free to go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's here. Can I say my bit from the car?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can, with the window down. I'll come beside you and give the line. Ten seconds; once you've answered, I release you to whatever the driver wants to discuss.

cards.title: Apologize Properly
cards.instruction: Get someone to deliver the apology in the form, order, and setting you consider valid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Please apologise for eating my cake at the table where it happened.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry. Does that help?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. It's a promising rehearsal. The cake plate is over there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your dad's sitting there. Can't we do this privately?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He watched me blame the dog. Tell him you ate it before you tell me you're sorry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Show me your apology email before you send it. The broken vase belongs in the subject line.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote 'sorry.' Can I leave it at that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can use that as the first word. Add what you broke; I'm not accepting an apology about your choice of font.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll write 'Sorry about the vase' to Mum. She still thinks you broke it. Can I send it now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After you start with 'I broke it.' My name comes out before your apology goes in. Read me that first sentence; then I'll decide whether it's ready.
